title: person
_what: ⛔ SNG-658 §2 — A PERSON YOU HAVE MET, as `character.npcRegistry` holds them. One schema per TYPE, not per file: an authored NPC and a met person are two types, and validating one against the other is how 133 of 133 registry people 'failed' the npc schema — `spectrum`, `fears` and `schemaVersion` are things an AUTHOR writes, which somebody you met in play has never had.
_derivedFrom: All 134 registry people across the 16 live saves, 2026-09-26. Each field's description says how often it is actually present, so the next reader knows which fields are the shape and which are the exceptions.
_forAevi: ⬜ §4.4 is yours: which of these are authored-only and belong in `npc` rather than here. My read from the corpus is that everything below is written BY PLAY — `domains`, `age`, `sex` and `appearance` are the ones a generator also fills, and `trueName`/`nameUnknown` exist precisely because a minted person carries a real name before the character learns it. Tighten `status` and `bondType`'s enums if the vocabulary is settled.

^_._what: a note or a provenance stamp, which is allowed to be anything — `_mergedFrom`, `_filledFromGenerate`, `_portraitTier`

id.description: 100% — the stable key this person is known by, for the life of the save. ⛔ Never re-coined when a name is revealed: the id stays and the display name changes (gm.js directive 14).

name.description: 100% — what the CHARACTER calls them, which is not always their real name. A person the character cannot yet name shows a label here and carries `trueName` beneath it.

role.description: 97% — what they do, in a few words. A role is not a name.

description.description: 97% — one line on who they are to look at.

firstMet.description: 97% — `{locationId, day}`: where and when the character first met them.

relationship.description: 97% — standing, running roughly −10..10. `relationshipBand` names the rungs: enemy · hostile · wary · neutral · friendly · ally · devoted.

history.description: 97% — what has passed between you, newest last, each line stamped with its day.

knownFacts.description: 97% — facts the character has learned about them.

skillsObserved.description: 97% — things the character has SEEN them do. Read by `contributionsOf` for what they bring to a fight or a watch.

status.description: 97% — active · injured · missing · dead · departed. ⛔ `dead` and `departed` are the two that mean GONE (CCODE-514): a keeper loses their post on these and on nothing else.

lastSeen.description: 88% — `{locationId, day}` of the most recent meeting.

statusNote.description: 80% — their CURRENT situation in one line, fed to the GM every turn so it is remembered rather than scrolling away.

gender.description: 80% — how they present. Separate from `sex` and gates nothing.

met.description: 78% — how many times the character has met them.

domains.description: 66% — the NPC sheet's domains, `{primary, …}`. Read for what they are made of.

domainsSource.description: 66% — where the domains came from: authored, derived, or generated.

sex.description: 31% — male · female · none. Set on first writing and never later; `none` is a real answer.

aliases.description: 18% — every prior name this person has gone by. ⛔ Matched exactly by `findExistingNpc`, which is what stops a re-introduction forking a second record.

nameRevealed.description: 13% — the fiction has given the character their real name.

age.description: 11% — years. The gate for every adult-only interaction; nothing infers it from prose.

peopleSource.description: 9% — where their people/kind was determined from.

people.description: 8% — the people or kind they belong to.

bondType.description: 7% — platonic · mentor · student · rival · family · romantic · sworn. ⛔ `sworn` outranks the band on both doors: a sworn person travels with you and comes forward at any standing (CCODE-511).

imagePinned.description: 7% — the player has fixed this portrait.

appearance.description: 7% — what they look like, for the portrait.

trueName.description: 7% — ⛔ their REAL name, carried from the moment they are minted and held back until the fiction reveals it. `findExistingNpc` matches it (CCODE-514) — without that, revealing a name forked a second record, which is exactly what happened to Orla Yardley.

nameUnknown.description: 5% — the character has not learned their name; `name` holds a label and `trueName` holds the truth.

creditedQuests.description: 4% — quests this person is credited on.

completions.description: 4% — how many pieces of work they have finished for the character.

roleSince.description: 3% — the day they took their current role.

questState.description: 3% — where they stand in a quest that involves them.

bondStage.description: 3% — a romantic bond's stage: courting · together · committed · partner. One step at a time.

imageSeedKey.description: 2% — the seed their portrait was drawn from, so it stays the same face.

formerIds.description: 1% — ids this person used to be keyed by. ⛔ Matched by `findExistingNpc`, so an op written against an old id still finds them.

linkedByReveal.description: 1% — the record this one was joined to when a name was revealed.

ally.description: 1% — a marker set by the quest path.

domainsNote.description: 1% — why their domains are what they are.

kin.description: 1% — a kinship or a sworn tie, in a word.

distinctFrom.description: rare — ids this person is explicitly NOT, so an op for the legend Sable never lands on the woman Sable (CCODE-423).

deathState.description: rare — set when they die: the depth they have sunk to, whether the way is held open, and whether they are sealed.

returnedFromDeath.description: rare — `{day, changed}` when somebody reached for them and the roll came back.

fateBy.description: rare — whose account of their death this was.

vouchedBy.description: rare — a known person who vouched for them in a scene.

carries.description: rare — items of the character's that they are holding.

teaches.description: rare — a tradition they can teach.

title.description: rare — their office or epithet, separate from the name: it is how a second Maren stays a different person.

fullName.description: rare — their whole name where the world's name pools have completed it.

pledge.description: rare — they said, aloud in a scene, that they would come for the character if death took them (SNG-653). A bond is not a promise.

deeds.description: rare — notable things THEY did that people would talk about, each with its day, place and weight. Not what passed between you two — that is .

wants.description: rare — what they want, which the world can act on.

npcId.description: rare — a legacy echo of `id` on a few older records.

worldLife.description: What the WORLD knows about this person that the character does not yet — a new role or a lesser status held beside what they know (`fates.js`), for the GM to let surface in the fiction, and cleared once what the character knows has caught up.

hurt.description: a wound this person took and has not yet put behind them — `{ day, by, why, cruel? }` (SNG-657 §3B). ⛑ Written when they stood against the leader of a raid and lost, and when a cruel power overran the place they kept. ⛔ HURT, NOT KILLED: a named defender lost to a line in a pass report is exactly what §3C forbids in the other direction, and a cruel escalation is the GM's beat to narrate. ⚠️ `additionalProperties` is false here, so a save whose keeper has been wounded would fail validation without this row.
